<thought>The spectrum shows a strong M peak at ~199, a prominent M+1 peak (~200.998) about 98 % of M, and a smaller M+2 peak (~202.001) about 9 % of M, with further decreasing peaks at +3, +4, +5. The clear M+1 pattern is characteristic of carbon (13C ≈1.1 % per carbon). No distinctive M+2 pattern of chlorine (≈33 % of M) or bromine (≈100 % of M) is present, so those elements cannot be definitively identified. Thus, the only element that can be definitively identified from the isotopic distribution is carbon.</thought>
<final_answer>['C']</final_answer>
